prompt:
You are judging pixel-art game assets for a game asset service.
The image shows 2 candidates labelled A, B for the same request. Each is enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling, so every square block is one pixel; the grey checkerboard stands for transparency.
The request was: A strigoi from Romanian folklore: a pale undead figure in a dark ragged cloak, side view facing left, standing. Canvas 32x32 pixels per frame, the body about the size of the central 26x26, inside a 3-pixel margin a pose may reach into.
Score every candidate:
- subject_read 1-5: how clearly it reads as the requested subject (5 instantly, 1 unrecognisable).
- craft 1-5: pixel-art craft: clean silhouette and outline, consistent shading and light, no noise, sensible use of the canvas (5 professional, 3 acceptable indie, 1 broken).
- consistency: 0 (single frame).
- verdict: ship (usable in a game as is), touch_up (usable after a few pixel fixes), redraw (not usable).
- note: one short sentence naming the main flaw or strength.
Then best: the label of the candidate you would ship; any_shippable: whether at least one is ship or touch_up.
Judge only what is visible.

reply.text: {"candidates": [{"label": "A", "subject_read": 3, "craft": 3, "consistency": 0, "verdict": "touch_up", "note": "Pale face and cloak read clearly, but the red hair is odd, the cloak isn't very ragged and the head is small next to a bulky body."}, {"label": "B", "subject_read": 4, "craft": 4, "consistency": 0, "verdict": "ship", "note": "The hooded pale face with red eye and clawed reaching hand reads strongly as a cloaked undead, with clean outline and shading."}], "best": "B", "any_shippable": true}
